stories.headline: Madras High Court rejects election petition filed against the victory of DMK former Minister S. Regupathy from Thirumayam
stories.title: Madras High Court rejects election petition filed against the victory of DMK former Minister S. Regupathy from Thirumayam
stories.summary: Justice G.K. Ilanthiraiyan rejects the election petition filed by TVK candidate C. Chinthamani who had lost by a margin of 1,492 votes
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The Madras High Court on Wednesday (September 30, 2026) rejected an election petition filed against the victory of Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) Member of the Legislative Assembly (MLA) S. Regupathy from Thirumayam constituency by a margin of 1,492 votes.

Justice G.K. Ilanthiraiyan allowed an application filed by the MLA to reject the election petition filed by Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) candidate C. Chinthamani at the threshold without forcing him to undergo the long drawn process of trial without there being any cause of action.

The judge agreed with the senior counsel P. Wilson, representing the MLA, that all allegations levelled against his client in the election petition were vague, scandalous, and vexatious besides having been made with the sole intention to defame and embarrass the legislator.

Ms. Chinthamani had challenged the election of Mr. Regupathy, also a former Minister in the DMK Cabinet, on the ground that the counting of votes cast in as many as 18 polling booths were not counted properly and that her plea for recounting of those votes was not accepted by the Returning Officer.

However, the judge held that the request was an afterthought since neither the election petitioner nor her counting agent had raised any objection during the counting of each round of votes but had raised the request for recounting only after knowing the margin of victory.
“A recount cannot be done as a matter of routine or course.
Unless the election petitioner provides clinching evidence to support their objections, a recount cannot be ordered.
Consequently, the representation submitted by the election petitioner was rightly rejected by the Returning officer,” the judge wrote.

In so far as the other ground that Mr. Regupathy had declared as many as 26 criminal cases pending against him in his 2021 election affidavit but did not declare even a single case in the 2026 affidavit, Justice Ilanthiraiyan said, the law does not mandate disclosure of cases that had been closed.
“Form 26 clearly stipulates that a candidate must disclose the pendency of criminal cases; it does not mandate the disclosure of closed or disposed criminal cases...
Therefore, the applicant had correctly stated that no criminal cases were pending against him as of the date of filing his nomination,” the judge ruled.

Further, stating that the election petitioner had failed to plead how the result of the election was materially affected, he recalled the Supreme Court as well as the High Court to have repeatedly held that a legislator could not be subjected to trial on the basis of a vague and unsubstantiated election petition.

stories.headline: The businesses redefining what’s possible in India
stories.title: The businesses redefining what’s possible in India
stories.summary: India’s next chapter of growth is not being written by any single sector. It is taking shape in art galleries and spice supply chains, in enzyme plants and hilltop resorts, in lecture halls and neighbourhood jewellery stores. What unites these stories is a willingness to question how things have always been done, whether that means making original art feel within reach, using technology to prove where a spice came from, or carrying a family legacy into a global export business. The leaders featured here come from very different worlds, but each is building something that widens what customers, communities and markets can expect from Indian enterprise.Aryaman Sethi: Changing How The World Buys ArtAryaman Sethi, Managing Director, AnYahh!! ArtIn India, original art is admired from a distance, not because it lacks appeal, but because it is perceived as unaffordable. Aryaman Sethi is challenging that assumption.As Managing Director of AnYahh!! Art, Sethi believes the journey to owning art begins with education, not a sales pitch. By helping people understand artists, styles, value and pricing, AnYahh!! replaces intimidation with confidence, and confidence with trust.With galleries in Delhi and Dubai, thousands of original works by Indian artists, free home consultations, rentals, EMI options, authenticity certificates and worldwide delivery, the brand is making art accessible and affordable without diminishing its value.For Sethi, the opportunity is larger than selling paintings. Every informed buyer can become a lifelong collector, while every collector creates visibility and opportunity for an artist. AnYahh!! is not asking India to spend more on art; it is showing people that original art was within reach all along.Follow here for more : https://www.instagram.com/anyahhartdelhi?stkn=MWgzcXEyZHgydzhmZA==Beyond the Spice Rack: Arshad Shajahan’s Ambition to Transform How India Sources, Trusts and Consumes SpicesArshad Shajahan, Founder, FLAVORA AiFor centuries, spices have travelled across borders and cultures. Yet for the consumer, much of their journey remains invisible.Arshad Shajahan wants to change that.Through FLAVORA Ai, which imports cassia, cloves, star anise and black pepper from Sri Lanka, Indonesia, Madagascar and Vietnam, Shajahan is building a technology-led spice company focused on traceability, food safety and smarter sourcing.“We don’t want to sell spices. We want consumers to know the story behind what they consume,” says Shajahan.His vision combines blockchain-based, batch-level traceability with QR-enabled transparency, allowing consumers to access information about origin and testing. AI could help identify adulteration risks and predict supply disruptions, while digital compliance can connect testing, customs and sourcing records.“We are not trying to make spices futuristic. We are trying to make the system behind them smarter,” he says.For Shajahan, the future of spices is about one thing: trust backed by evidence.Dr. Arpit Chopra Jain: Advancing a Modern Vision for HomeopathyDr. Arpit Chopra JainDr. Arpit Chopra Jain, M.D. (Homeopathy) and recipient of an Honorary Doctorate from the USA, is a distinguished homeopathic practitioner committed to expanding awareness and understanding of homeopathy. Dr Arpit Chopra Jain (MD Homoeopathy) Director of Aarogya Super Speciality Modern Homoeopathic Clinic Indore & Representative of Homeopathic Medicine for BRICS Countries at BCMFHe is associated with the renowned Aarogya Super Speciality Modern Homeopathic Clinic, where his work focuses on managing complex and chronic health conditions through homeopathic approaches.Over the course of his professional journey, Dr. Jain has received recognition from prominent Indian dignitaries, including Ex Vice President of India Jagdeep Dhankhar and Union Health Minister J. P. Nadda.A central part of Dr. Jain’s mission is to challenge misconceptions surrounding homeopathy and encourage greater discussion about its potential role in healthcare. His clinical work has particularly focused on patients with serious and complex conditions, including cases where surgical intervention may otherwise be considered.According to his professional profile, Dr. Jain has treated more than 3,000 complex cases. He plans to systematically compile and present treatment data to the World Health Organization (WHO) in the future, with the aim of contributing to broader international discussion and research concerning homeopathy.Through clinical practice, documentation and international engagement, Dr. Arpit Chopra Jain continues to pursue his vision of bringing greater global attention to homeopathy while advocating for evidence, research and wider professional dialogue.Arun Raam GowdaBuilding experience-led businesses while creating impact through entrepreneurship, innovation and community initiatives.Arun Raam Gowda, Actor, Entrepreneur and PhilanthropistActor | Entrepreneur | PhilanthropistArun Raam Gowda is an actor, entrepreneur, and philanthropist building a strong presence across hospitality, technology, entertainment, and social impact. Based in Bengaluru, he is known for creating experience-led ventures that blend innovation with customer-first thinking.Also known as Aru Gowda and Arun Gowda, his hospitality journey spans award-winning restaurants, breweries, lounges, and experiential destinations, including Atlantis Brewery, Sugar Factory Reloaded, and Bangalore Adda.Beyond hospitality, Gowda is actively building technology-driven ventures while continuing his association with cinema, bringing together business, creativity, and storytelling.He is the founder of the Arun Raam Foundation, which supports initiatives in education, healthcare, youth empowerment, disaster relief, and humanitarian assistance. During the COVID-19 pandemic, the foundation’s Surprise Van initiative delivered essential supplies and emergency support to those in need.Through his multi-industry journey, Arun Raam Gowda continues to unite entrepreneurship, innovation, entertainment, and meaningful social impact.https://share.google/EVoy5v64762b5YHlzDr M Nadeem Zafar Clinician and Faculty, Clinical PsychiatryDr M Nadeem Zafar, Academic Director, Arise Medical Academy, Faculty, DocTutorialsDr Zafar is a clinician and educator in clinical psychiatry, celebrated for a teaching style that is as engaging as fun to grasp . His ability to make complex clinical concepts memorable has made him a sought-after faculty member across borders.An internationally renowned educator, he has taught in ten countries and has spoken on global platforms, including the United Nations (SDG, 2023).He has been tagged as one of the most influential medical mentors. And recently he has been selected for the world leaders submit 2026, Oxford, UK for “Excellence in Medical Education and Academic Leadership Award”Mr. Ajay Badekar Director – Stone Water by ZuperAjay Badekar brings years of hospitality expertise to Stone Water Resort & Spa, blending international-inspired design, distinctive experiences and warm Indian hospitality in Karjat.Ajay Badekar, Director, Stone Water Resort & Spa, KarjatMr. Ajay Badekar’s entrepreneurial journey in hospitality has been shaped by a simple belief: memorable stays are created through experiences that go beyond the ordinary. For eight years, his Forest Club Resort in Karjat has redefined the hilltop getaway experience, featuring one of the country’s largest meandering pools. Its strong patron response inspired him to envision newer, more distinctive hospitality concepts.His connection with hospitality began much earlier through his family’s ancestral restaurant, Namak. Over the last 12 years, under his leadership, Namak has evolved into Karjat’s signature dining destination, celebrated for its untouched gourmet experiences and excellent hospitality.Today, as Director of Stone Water Resort & Spa, Karjat, Mr. Badekar is bringing this vision to a larger canvas, introducing international-inspired infrastructure and a distinctive resort lifestyle to Karjat. Inspired by Bali, its unique multi-layered pool concept is among its defining experiences. More than a resort, Stone Water is envisioned as a sanctuary of leisure, luxury and warmth for vacations, weddings and celebrations.Manoj Alankar Mandir: Adding Sparkle to India’s Most Memorable MomentsManoj Kumar, Founder, Manoj Alankar MandirManoj Alankar Mandir is bringing together tradition, elegance and contemporary jewellery choices for customers in Sikandarpur, Ballia. Founded by Manoj Kumar, the business has established itself as a destination for jewellery suited to weddings, festivals, celebrations, gifting and everyday wear. From necklaces and earrings to bangles, rings and mangalsutras, customers can explore a wide variety of designs under one roof. What further makes the experience attractive is the 5% making charges offer on all kinds of jewellery. By combining timeless Indian traditions with evolving style preferences, Manoj Alankar Mandir is making jewellery shopping more accessible and versatile. Every piece represents more than fashion—it becomes part of celebrations, memories and life's most meaningful moments.Follow here : https://www.instagram.com/manojalankarmandir?stkn=cm52ZmR6MW55ZDk4&utm_source=qrConclusionTaken together, these seven journeys show that redefining what’s possible rarely begins with scale. It begins with a clear belief about trust, access, experience or knowledge, and the discipline to build around it. From Delhi and Dubai to Bengaluru, Karjat and Ballia, these leaders are proving that ambition in India is no longer confined to its largest cities or most familiar industries. As their businesses grow, they are also raising the bar for the enterprises that will follow.The pages slugged ‘Brand Connect’ are equivalent to advertisements and are not written and produced by Forbes India journalists.

stories.headline: What happens when experience meets a different way of thinking: Leadership stories across the new economy
stories.title: What happens when experience meets a different way of thinking: Leadership stories across the new economy
stories.summary: Business is increasingly being shaped by people who approach familiar problems differently. Across education, nutrition, pharma, real estate and India’s startup ecosystem, these five leaders are building around ideas that extend beyond conventional playbooks. Their stories are distinct, but share a common thread: each has drawn on experience, identified a gap and chosen to build with a clear point of view. Here are five leadership journeys worth looking at more closely.Ayush Khandelwal & Deepak Sahu: Building Toppersclubs Around What JEE and NEET Aspirants Actually NeedAyush Khandelwal and Deepak Sahu, Co-Founders of Toppersclubs, came to the same problem from two very different experiences with the education system.Khandelwal, a B.Tech graduate in Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning, also founded EliteCreatorsHub.com, an influencer marketing agency that has crossed 500 million views for brands with strong ROI, bootstrapped and profitable from day one. That experience gave him hands-on acumen across content, technology and growth, and an instinct for turning complex problems into simple systems.Sahu took a different route. He cleared NEET on his first attempt in 2021, securing AIR 5, and soon after began mentoring students on YouTube, quickly becoming one of the most recognisable voices for the exam online. His channel has since crossed 190,000 subscribers and reaches over a million students monthly. Having cracked it himself, on the first try, Sahu understood not just how to prepare for NEET, but how to actually become a topper, an understanding that would go on to shape Toppersclubs.Four years ago, that mix of business discipline and on-ground insight led to a simple bet: aspirants don’t need more content, they need guidance from people who’ve actually cracked the exam. Like Khandelwal’s earlier venture, Toppersclubs was built bootstrapped and profitable from day one, growing from Sahu’s own mentoring into a network of 20+ toppers ranked AIR 1 to 100, now backed by its own app.Students can build a custom test by choosing exactly which chapters or subjects to practice. The platform tracks each student’s patterns, slow topics, guessed answers, recurring mistakes, and pushes more questions from weak areas. An All India Test Series lets them benchmark against every serious aspirant nationwide.The real shift: a page-wise NCERT question set built by subject experts alongside NEET toppers ranked AIR 1 to 25, built the way no test series has been built before.For Khandelwal and Sahu, the principle stays simple: the right person to guide a topper is someone who has already been one.Vikram Salwan: Bringing QNT’s European Sports Nutrition Expertise to the Indian ConsumerWith nine companies across technology, electronics and software behind him, Vikram Salwan brings an engineer’s approach to QNT – Quality Nutrition Technology. A Belgium-based sports nutrition brand, QNT is Salwan’s passion project in India, where he holds the business rights and has taken a hands-on role in shaping its manufacturing, supply chain, product development and quality standards.For Salwan, building a sustainable business matters more than chasing scale at any cost. His focus is on creating products that earn consumer trust and bring people back, rather than relying heavily on discounts or rising acquisition spends. That thinking has also led QNT to maintain its own manufacturing and supply chain in India, giving the brand greater control over the product journey.The brand is CoE-NSTS certified and tested against more than 220 WADA-banned substances, reinforcing its emphasis on quality and transparency. QNT’s focus on high-protein formulations is also evident across its range, with even its regular protein line offering 75% protein, a level of protein concentration that many major brands position as an isolate-level proposition.That consumer-first approach is reflected in QNT ISO Ripped Whey Isolate Protein, an exclusive QNT formulation for Indian consumers. The product combines 32g of whey protein isolate with L-Carnitine, and CLA bringing multiple functional ingredients into a single formula. With its isolate-led formulation and composition focused on protein intake, it is also positioned as a strong choice for consumers following GLP-1-based weight-management approaches, where maintaining adequate protein intake can be an important consideration.For Salwan, ISO Ripped represents more than a product addition to QNT’s portfolio. It reflects his belief that international nutrition brands should not simply bring existing products to India, but understand the local consumer and develop products around their needs.His larger ambition is to make quality sports nutrition accessible beyond elite athletes, reaching competitive performers, everyday gym-goers and first-time fitness consumers alike.Kapil Aggarwal: Building a More Connected Future for Pharma ResearchPharma research has become more sophisticated, but some of the everyday challenges inside laboratories remain surprisingly familiar. Data sits across different systems, teams work with separate workflows, and researchers can spend valuable time looking for information instead of working with it.For Kapil Aggarwal, Regional VP of Sales for India and South Asia at Revvity Signals, this is a challenge he has encountered throughout more than a decade in scientific software sales and consulting. His experience includes leadership roles at PerkinElmer Informatics and Cambridgesoft Corp, as well as work in IT education and scientific consulting.That experience has shaped a straightforward view of technology: it should make research easier, not add another layer of complexity.At ETPharma’s Lab of the Future roundtable, Aggarwal discussed SignalsOne, Revvity Signals’ platform designed to bring research data and workflows into a more connected environment. The platform helps teams organise information, search across experiments, automate parts of their workflows and support report generation, addressing some of the time researchers lose navigating fragmented systems.Kapil’s work, however, extends beyond the technology itself. He works with CEOs, CIOs and research teams on the practical realities of adoption, including training, data migration and governance.As AI, cloud systems, and analytics become increasingly embedded in pharma R&D, his focus remains grounded in the researcher’s experience: technology should give scientists more time to interpret, investigate, and advance their work, rather than spend it managing information.Shekhar Agrawal: Shri Divine Group and the Emergence of Spiritual Real Estate in IndiaFor Shekhar Agrawal, Director of Shri Group and Shri Divine Group, real estate has never been only about constructing buildings. His approach begins with a broader question: What should a space give back to the people who live in it?Founded in 1997, Shri Group has built a significant presence across the Mathura–Vrindavan region, with a development footprint spanning approximately 750 acres. This journey has shaped Agrawal’s understanding of real estate as something that extends beyond construction,bringing together people, place and the environment they inhabit.Shri Divine Group represents the next evolution of this philosophy, exploring a more spiritually conscious approach to real estate where modern living and inner well-being can coexist.Agrawal believes the future of premium real estate will be increasingly experiential. While quality construction, thoughtful architecture, infrastructure and timely execution remain essential, elements such as natural surroundings, openness, tranquillity and a sense of belonging can significantly influence how people experience their homes.This vision becomes particularly relevant in Vrindavan and the wider Braj region, where culture, spirituality and everyday life have remained deeply connected for centuries. Agrawal sees an opportunity to create developments that respect this distinctive identity while meeting the expectations of modern buyers.It is here that his idea of “Spiritual Real Estate” takes shape, spaces designed not merely as assets, but as environments where material comfort and inner well-being can coexist.For Shri Divine Group, the journey ahead is about creating places that feel intentional, purposeful and connected to their surroundings.“The next evolution of luxury will not be defined only by what a development offers, but by how it makes people feel,” shares, Shekhar Agrawal, Director, Shri Group & Shri Divine Group.Wing Commander Anthony Anish: From the Cockpit to India’s Startup EcosystemFrom the cockpit of an IAF helicopter to the boardrooms of India’s startup ecosystem, Wing Commander Anthony Anish (Retd) has carried one idea through his career: leadership matters most when situations are uncertain.An alumnus of the National Defence Academy, Anish began his operational career at 21, flying helicopters during the Kargil War in 1999 and the Siachen operation in 2002. His experience expanded to disaster response during the 2014 Jammu & Kashmir floods, and to frontier technology through his role in the development of the Rustom-1 drone for DRDO.After 20 years in the Indian Air Force, he moved into entrepreneurship and was part of the founding team of India's largest residential community App, MyGate. The experience led him to a larger ambition of building the ecosystem around startups, not just individual companies. As Chief Operating Officer of T-Hub, Anish scaled the innovation hub from 250 startups to more than 2,000. During his tenure, T-Hub startups raised more than ₹20,000 crore and created over 75,000 jobs, while the organisation itself received the national award for Best Indian Incubator for all the years during his tenure.Today, his work spans across defence innovation, venture building and mentorship. opening: Business is increasingly being shaped by people who approach familiar problems differently.
Across education, nutrition, pharma, real estate and India’s startup ecosystem, these five leaders are building around ideas that extend beyond conventional playbooks.
body: Their stories are distinct, but share a common thread: each has drawn on experience, identified a gap and chosen to build with a clear point of view.
Here are five leadership journeys worth looking at more closely.
Ayush Khandelwal & Deepak Sahu: Building Toppersclubs Around.
What JEE and NEET Aspirants Actually NeedAyush Khandelwal and Deepak Sahu, Co-Founders of Toppersclubs, came to the same problem from two very different experiences with the education system.

Khandelwal, a B.Tech graduate in Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning, also founded EliteCreatorsHub.com, an influencer marketing agency that has crossed 500 million views for brands with strong ROI, bootstrapped and profitable from day one.
That experience gave him hands-on acumen across content, technology and growth, and an instinct for turning complex problems into simple systems.
Sahu took a different route.
He cleared NEET on his first attempt in 2021, securing AIR 5, and soon after began mentoring students on YouTube, quickly becoming one of the most recognisable voices for the exam online.
His channel has since crossed 190,000 subscribers and reaches over a million students monthly.
Having cracked it himself, on the first try, Sahu understood not just how to prepare for NEET, but how to actually become a topper, an understanding that would go on to shape Toppersclubs.
Four years ago, that mix of business discipline and on-ground insight led to a simple bet: aspirants don’t need more content, they need guidance from people who’ve actually cracked the exam.

Like Khandelwal’s earlier venture, Toppersclubs was built bootstrapped and profitable from day one, growing from Sahu’s own mentoring into a network of 20+ toppers ranked AIR 1 to 100, now backed by its own app.
Students can build a custom test by choosing exactly which chapters or subjects to practice.
The platform tracks each student’s patterns, slow topics, guessed answers, recurring mistakes, and pushes more questions from weak areas.
An All India Test Series lets them benchmark against every serious aspirant nationwide.
The real shift: a page-wise NCERT question set built by subject experts alongside NEET toppers ranked AIR 1 to 25, built the way no test series has been built before.
For Khandelwal and Sahu, the principle stays simple: the right person to guide a topper is someone who has already been one.

Vikram Salwan: Bringing QNT’s European Sports Nutrition Expertise to the Indian ConsumerWith nine companies across technology, electronics and software behind him, Vikram Salwan brings an engineer’s approach to QNT – Quality Nutrition Technology.

A Belgium-based sports nutrition brand, QNT is Salwan’s passion project in India, where he holds the business rights and has taken a hands-on role in shaping its manufacturing, supply chain, product development and quality standards.
For Salwan, building a sustainable business matters more than chasing scale at any cost.
His focus is on creating products that earn consumer trust and bring people back, rather than relying heavily on discounts or rising acquisition spends.
That thinking has also led QNT to maintain its own manufacturing and supply chain in India, giving the brand greater control over the product journey.
The brand is CoE-NSTS certified and tested against more than 220 WADA-banned substances, reinforcing its emphasis on quality and transparency.

QNT’s focus on high-protein formulations is also evident across its range, with even its regular protein line offering 75% protein, a level of protein concentration that many major brands position as an isolate-level proposition.
That consumer-first approach is reflected in QNT ISO Ripped Whey Isolate Protein, an exclusive QNT formulation for Indian consumers.
The product combines 32g of whey protein isolate with L-Carnitine, and CLA bringing multiple functional ingredients into a single formula.

With its isolate-led formulation and composition focused on protein intake, it is also positioned as a strong choice for consumers following GLP-1-based weight-management approaches, where maintaining adequate protein intake can be an important consideration.
For Salwan, ISO Ripped represents more than a product addition to QNT’s portfolio.
It reflects his belief that international nutrition brands should not simply bring existing products to India, but understand the local consumer and develop products around their needs.
His larger ambition is to make quality sports nutrition accessible beyond elite athletes, reaching competitive performers, everyday gym-goers and first-time fitness consumers alike.

Kapil Aggarwal: Building a More Connected Future for Pharma ResearchPharma research has become more sophisticated, but some of the everyday challenges inside laboratories remain surprisingly familiar.
Data sits across different systems, teams work with separate workflows, and researchers can spend valuable time looking for information instead of working with it.
For Kapil Aggarwal, Regional VP of Sales for India and South Asia at Revvity Signals, this is a challenge he has encountered throughout more than a decade in scientific software sales and consulting.
His experience includes leadership roles at PerkinElmer Informatics and Cambridgesoft Corp, as well as work in IT education and scientific consulting.
That experience has shaped a straightforward view of technology: it should make research easier, not add another layer of complexity.
At ETPharma’s Lab of the Future roundtable, Aggarwal discussed Signals.
One, Revvity Signals’ platform designed to bring research data and workflows into a more connected environment.

The platform helps teams organise information, search across experiments, automate parts of their workflows and support report generation, addressing some of the time researchers lose navigating fragmented systems.
Kapil’s work, however, extends beyond the technology itself.
He works with CEOs, CIOs and research teams on the practical realities of adoption, including training, data migration and governance.

As AI, cloud systems, and analytics become increasingly embedded in pharma R&D, his focus remains grounded in the researcher’s experience: technology should give scientists more time to interpret, investigate, and advance their work, rather than spend it managing information.

Shekhar Agrawal: Shri Divine Group and the Emergence of Spiritual Real Estate in IndiaFor Shekhar Agrawal, Director of Shri Group and Shri Divine Group, real estate has never been only about constructing buildings.
His approach begins with a broader question: What should a space give back to the people who live in it?
Founded in 1997, Shri Group has built a significant presence across the Mathura–Vrindavan region, with a development footprint spanning approximately 750 acres.
This journey has shaped Agrawal’s understanding of real estate as something that extends beyond construction,bringing together people, place and the environment they inhabit.
Shri Divine Group represents the next evolution of this philosophy, exploring a more spiritually conscious approach to real estate where modern living and inner well-being can coexist.
Agrawal believes the future of premium real estate will be increasingly experiential.

While quality construction, thoughtful architecture, infrastructure and timely execution remain essential, elements such as natural surroundings, openness, tranquillity and a sense of belonging can significantly influence how people experience their homes.
This vision becomes particularly relevant in Vrindavan and the wider Braj region, where culture, spirituality and everyday life have remained deeply connected for centuries.
Agrawal sees an opportunity to create developments that respect this distinctive identity while meeting the expectations of modern buyers.
It is here that his idea of “Spiritual Real Estate” takes shape, spaces designed not merely as assets, but as environments where material comfort and inner well-being can coexist.
For Shri Divine Group, the journey ahead is about creating places that feel intentional, purposeful and connected to their surroundings.
“The next evolution of luxury will not be defined only by what a development offers, but by how it makes people feel,” shares, Shekhar Agrawal, Director, Shri Group & Shri Divine Group.

Wing Commander Anthony Anish: From the Cockpit to India’s Startup EcosystemFrom the cockpit of an IAF helicopter to the boardrooms of India’s startup ecosystem, Wing Commander Anthony Anish (Retd) has carried one idea through his career: leadership matters most when situations are uncertain.
An alumnus of the National Defence Academy, Anish began his operational career at 21, flying helicopters during the Kargil War in 1999 and the Siachen operation in 2002.
His experience expanded to disaster response during the 2014 Jammu & Kashmir floods, and to frontier technology through his role in the development of the Rustom-1 drone for DRDO.
After 20 years in the Indian Air Force, he moved into entrepreneurship and was part of the founding team of India's largest residential community App, MyGate.
The experience led him to a larger ambition of building the ecosystem around startups, not just individual companies.
As Chief Operating Officer of T-Hub, Anish scaled the innovation hub from 250 startups to more than 2,000.

During his tenure, T-Hub startups raised more than ₹20,000 crore and created over 75,000 jobs, while the organisation itself received the national award for Best Indian Incubator for all the years during his tenure.
Today, his work spans across defence innovation, venture building and mentorship.
He is a partner at Tetris Ventures, serves as a Board of director on ICSI (Institute of Company Secretaries of India) for startups and partner of a defence-focused venture capital fund.
He has also represented India at international forums like the G20, SCO and the Hon Prime Minister Narender Modi’s INDUS-X delegation to the US.
For Anish, the transition from uniform to business is another form of nation-building, using experience in crisis, technology and execution to help create the next generation of Indian enterprises.

stories.headline: Indian Cabinet approves 1-10% hike in rabi crops minimum support price
stories.title: Indian Cabinet approves 1-10% hike in rabi crops minimum support price
stories.summary: MSP for wheat now stands at ₹2,610 per quintal against ₹2,585 per quintal announced for 2026-27 marketing season (April-March)
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'cabinet approves' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Indian government announced minimum support prices (MSPs) for the rabi marketing season 2027-28 after the Cabinet approved 1-10 per cent hike on Wednesday, a day before the winter sowing season is set to commence.
The lowest hike in wheat was less than 1 per cent while the highest was for safflower by 10.3 per cent.
After the revision, the MSP of winter season’s main cereal wheat now stands at ₹2,610 per quintal against ₹2,585 per quintal announced for 2026-27 marketing season (April-March).

Briefing media after the Cabinet meeting, Information and Broadcasting Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said that the Cabinet approved the MSPs recommendations of the Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices (CACP) as proposed by the agriculture ministry.
“The production cost of wheat is ₹1,264 per quintal, but MSP has been kept more than double at ₹2,610 per quintal for 2027-28,” he said.

Among other rabi crops, barley MSP has been increased by 6.3 per cent to ₹2,286 per quintal from ₹2,150 per quintal, gram (chana) has been hiked by 1.4 per cent to ₹5,958 per quintal from ₹5,875 per quintal, lentil (masur) by 5.6 per cent to ₹7,390 per quintal from ₹7,000 per quintal, mustard by 6.7 per cent to ₹6,613 per quintal from ₹6,200 per quintal and safflower to ₹7,215 per quintal from ₹6,540 per quintal, an official statement said.

Total payout to farmers is estimated to be ₹90,962 crore for 324 lakh tonnes in the 2027-28 marketing year, the minister said adding the MSPs have been decided factoring the cost of production, El Nino concerns, and global and domestic price trends.

The government has fixed a production target of 177.72 million tonnes (mt) of foodgrains which includes 121 mt of wheat, 17.20 mt of pulses and 22.30 mt of nutri/coarse cereals during current rabi season.
As the monsoon rainfall during whole of September was only 8 per cent deficient, some parts may be able to have adequate moisture for sowing.

However, some states which have received 20 per cent or more deficit rainfall in September may have to depend entirely for canal irrigation amid forecast of further strengthening of El Nino in the coming months.
During September, Maharashtra reported 52 per cent deficit rainfall, Karnataka -57 per cent, Telangana -24 per cent, Punjab -64 per cent and Haryana -44 per cent.

Satyam Shivam Sundaram, Partner, Strategy & Transactions, EY LLP, said the higher MSP increases for oilseeds and pulses, coupled with a relatively modest increase for wheat, reflect a calibrated policy shift towards crop diversification, import substitution, and a broader move from a food security centric approach towards nutrition security.

stories.headline: Modi, Trump review bilateral ties amid concerns over Russia sanctions
stories.title: Modi, Trump review bilateral ties amid concerns over Russia sanctions
stories.summary: ‘We agreed to maintain close engagement to take our Comprehensive Global Strategic Partnership forward’, said Prime Minister Narendra Modi in a post on X
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: In their first telephone call since the United States (U.S.) Congress passed the new Russian sanctions law, Prime Minister Narendra Modi said he and President Donald Trump had a “productive conversation” and reviewed bilateral ties.

Mr. Modi and Mr. Trump spoke amid growing concerns over the India-U.S. relationship, underlined by a talk by External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar in New York earlier this week where he spelt out a number of “issues”, including over tariffs, FTA negotiations, the U.S.’s treatment of Indian migrants and Pakistan.
Data Story | 100% U.S. tariff threat: Can India’s new trade deals reduce its dependence on America?

The call between the two leaders followed talks between Mr. Jaishankar and U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio as well as Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri and U.S. Undersecretary of State Allison Hooker on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA).

During both meetings, Indian officials had raised concerns over the U.S.’s new Lindsey O Graham Sanctions Against Russia and Iran Act (SRIA), which mandates Mr. Trump to levy up to 100% tariffs on goods imported from India, China and other countries that import Russian oil.
Mr. Misri also raised the issues with a U.S. Congressional delegation in Delhi this week.
In a social media post, Mr. Modi said he and Mr. Trump discussed India-U.S. cooperation in “trade, defence, energy, critical technologies and other areas”, but made no direct reference to the SRIA.
“We agreed to maintain close engagement to take our Comprehensive Global Strategic Partnership forward.
We also exchanged views on regional and international issues, including ongoing efforts to advance global peace and security,” he said.
On December 14-15, Mr. Modi is expected to travel to Florida to attend the G20 summit hosted by Mr. Trump.

Officials said it was too early to confirm whether Mr. Modi, who will travel to Canada prior to that, would also hold bilateral talks with Mr. Trump, and indicated that the progress in the talks for the Free Trade Agreement (FTA), which the U.S. is keen to complete quickly, could determine the engagement.

At a talk at the Asia Society in New York this week, Mr. Jaishankar acknowledged that New Delhi had several pending issues with the U.S., although he said “much of the world has had a more difficult relationship with the U.S.” as well.
